findings.F1: The tested effect is not in the explored folds: inside the falling calm profile, the next-day excess return does not fall as the 30-day fall gets deeper. The deepest quintile of the 30-day fall (in units of 20-day swing, mean -1.59) returned +0.05 % (t 0.12, 170 days), against -0.57 % (t -1.49) for the second quintile and -0.29 % (t -0.87) for the shallowest. The idea's size, +0.13 % unusual move (t 0.51), is under the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: Where a day closes in its own high-low range predicts the next day the opposite way, across all bars. The graded reversal signal (0.5 minus the close's position in the range) times the next-day excess return averaged +0.089 % with t 3.04 over 1,448 days. Closes in the lowest fifth of the range were followed by +0.59 % (t 2.40, 592 days) and closes in the highest fifth by -0.34 % (t -1.65, 635 days). The effect fades with time: t 1.68 at 2 days and -0.33 at 3 days.
findings.F3: The close-near-the-low rebound is about 0.10 of the coin's usual daily move (1,597 cases), about three times the tested idea's 0.030. Its +0.59 % per case is about 3 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F4: The close-location reversal lives in the more agitated stretches. When the 20-day swing was above its window median, a close in the lowest quarter of the range was followed by +1.16 % (t 3.14, 311 days) and a close in the top quarter by -0.63 % (t -2.55, 421 days). When the swing was below that median, the same reads were +0.05 % (t 0.16) and -0.19 % (t -0.82). Inside the falling calm profile they were +0.08 % (t 0.21) and -0.28 % (t -0.95).
findings.F5: The rebound grows with the width of the day. Among the widest third of days (range over 20-day swing), a close in the lowest quarter was followed by +1.10 % (t 2.71, 246 days), against +0.17 % (t 0.44) and -0.03 % (t -0.08) in the narrower two thirds.
findings.F6: The rebound appears on every coin and in both halves of the explored windows, though not significantly everywhere. Low-close next-day means were positive on all six coins, from +0.17 % (ETH) to +0.93 % (XMR, t 3.21). They were +0.87 % (t 2.14) in w13-18 and +0.20 % (t 0.64) in w7-12.
findings.F7: The day's own return, scaled by its 20-day swing, also reverses the next day (graded t 2.29, 1,209 days). The most down-scaled fifth of days was followed by +0.66 % (t 2.24) and the fourth fifth by -0.46 % (t -2.30). This is the same rebound seen through the close rather than the range. Weekday, volatility rank and the 30-day trend outside the profile showed nothing beyond t 2.3, among about 20 angles looked at.

ideas.idea: The lower a coin closes within its day's high-low range, the more it rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A daily close near the day's low is a reason to buy, or to stop shorting, for one day, and a close near the high a reason not to chase.
ideas.name: low close rebounds next day

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the lower a coin closes within its day's high-low range, the more it rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: The close-near-the-low rebound is worth trading when the coin swings more than usual for it, where it is several times the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: agitated low close rebound

ideas.idea: The wider a day's high-low range against the coin's daily swing over the past 20 days, and the nearer its close to the low, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A wide day that ends near its low marks exhausted selling, and the coin is a one-day buy.
ideas.name: wide day low close rebound
